A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study of differentially private federated learning for speech recognition. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices support reliable comparison despite the changed title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech-recognition training experiments, WER comparisons and clipping analyses in the main text and appendices. Population-scale privacy extrapolations are distinguished from measured results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experiments and reports additional cohort-size, clipping and privacy–utility results, including Tables 16 and 20.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 generalizes uniform cohort averaging to prescribed client weights with 1/q normalization and corresponding weight-dependent noise scaling. Experiments still use uniform weights. The CTC transformer, local SGD/server LAMB recipe and both per-layer clipping rules are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use LibriSpeech and Common Voice v13.0, covering English, French and German, heterogeneous/randomized client partitions and the same seed-model domain-transfer scenarios. Added cohort and noise settings do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 8, 9 and 13 retain the same optimizer and FedProx comparisons. Global, uniform per-layer and dimension-based clipping comparisons also remain. Newly cited methods and theoretical comparisons do not establish additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds French/German cohorts of 128, extends cohort sweeps to 5,120 using the existing 10-local-step procedure, and adds central-training controls with three times the batch size (Table 16). Table 20 reports an LS-960-seed DP sweep at cohort 1,024. Core splits, metrics and training recipes remain stable; the main tables’ changed noise units reflect reparameterization.

E4.justification: Appendix H.10 extends cohort-scaling analysis with larger cohorts and central-batch controls. Tables 17 and 20 add clipping-sensitivity and LS-960-seed noise/clipping evidence. These extend existing questions; the earlier architecture, augmentation, FedProx, seed-quality and layer-specific noise ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report mean and standard deviation in gradient/delta summaries, without repeated-run WER uncertainty, seed counts, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new theoretical variance terms do not change empirical uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds WER entries in Tables 10, 16, 17 and 20; for example, Table 16 reports 16.9% test WER for LS-100-to-CV-en training at cohort 5,120, an added setting. In the retained zero-noise, C=1 row, per-layer dev/test WER changes from 15.9/19.1 to 15.7/18.9 (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 1). Most earlier results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v1 provides DP definitions, clipping definitions and a restated privacy-accounting theorem. v2 adds substantial original convergence analysis: smoothness and variance assumptions, clipping lemmas, Theorems 2 and 3 for full and partial participation, Corollary 1, detailed proofs and claimed recovery of prior bounds (Section 3 and Appendix F).

C1.justification: v2 makes convergence guarantees and the joint role of clipping and layer-wise normalization central contributions, and claims broader guidance for large-model FL beyond ASR. v1 primarily emphasizes the benchmark and empirical training recipe. The headline extrapolated privacy/WER results were already present in v1.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds substantive interpretations involving clipping bias, trust ratios, within/across-client variance, training duration and DP-noise trade-offs. Appendix H.10 adds a seed-overfitting explanation, and Appendix I.6 discusses why clipping benefits differ from NLP findings. Appendix I.3 also changes the noise-invariance explanation inconsistently.

D1.justification: v2 newly clarifies speaker-disjoint splits and validation/test speaker-duration statistics, and documents settings for the added scaling experiments. Existing preprocessing, architecture, hardware and compute disclosures are largely retained or relocated. Both versions only promise a future code release.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning around adaptive clipping, convergence and deep-model divergence, adding works including Chan et al., Shulgin and Richtarik, Xiao et al. and He et al. It claims a first convergence bound combining LAMB, per-layer clipping and DP, and explicitly credits prior ASR work for training from scratch within 2,000 central steps.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Related work moves after experiments, empirical setup and results are combined, and implementation details, Algorithm 1 and ethics/reproducibility statements move into reorganized appendices. Author information and a contributions statement also change.

P2.justification: Most plots retain their visual content. v2 extends Figure 3, adds Tables 16 and 20, expands existing tables and relocates the speaker-statistics table. The separate v1 Figure 6 disappears, but its training curves remain within the appendix plots. Figures, captions and surrounding layout are adjusted.

improvement.justification: The added scaling controls and privacy–utility results strengthen the empirical evidence. However, the central new convergence claim has an unresolved inconsistency: Corollary 1 requires positive kappa, while its stated diminishing local learning rate makes kappa negative as training duration grows with fixed local steps. Appendix I.3 also replaces v1’s constant C/σ condition with constant Cσ_DP while retaining an incompatible halving-both example. These problems limit confidence in the theoretical and explanatory gains, leaving the net quality change uncertain.
